description: Mint a short-lived, single-use URL that this server serves for uploading a file as an attachment to a draft message or an event, or as a file in a OneDrive/SharePoint folder, so the bytes go straight from the caller to Microsoft Graph instead of passing as base64 through the agent context. target is the attachments collection of the item: /me/messages/{message-id}/attachments (a draft; create it first) or /me/events/{event-id}/attachments; or a drive folder: /me/drive/root, /me/drive/items/{folder-id}, /drives/{drive-id}/items/{folder-id}, /sites/{site-id}/drive/items/{folder-id}. PUT the raw file bytes to the returned uploadUrl with a Content-Length (e.g. curl -T file ""); the response confirms the upload. Up to 150 MB. Pass contentId to attach inline, e.g. a signature picture the HTML body shows with . For a drive folder, conflictBehavior says what happens when the name is taken (default fail; contentId does not apply). Requires --enable-attachment-urls. Returns { uploadUrl, method, expiresAt, singleUse, maxBytes, conflictBehavior? }.

conflictBehavior.description: Drive folder targets only: what happens when the folder already has a file with this name. fail (default), replace, or rename.

contentId.description: Attach inline under this Content-ID instead of as a regular attachment, so the HTML body can show the file with , e.g. a picture in an email signature. Letters, digits, ".", "_", "@", "-".

contentType.description: MIME type of the file, e.g. application/pdf. Defaults to application/octet-stream.

name.description: File name as it will be stored, e.g. report.pdf: the attachment name, or the file name in the drive folder.

target.description: Attachments collection of a draft message or an event, e.g. /me/messages/{message-id}/attachments, /me/events/{event-id}/attachments, or /users/{user-id}/messages/{message-id}/attachments for another mailbox. Or a OneDrive/SharePoint folder: /me/drive/root, /me/drive/items/{folder-id}, /drives/{drive-id}/items/{folder-id}, /sites/{site-id}/drive/items/{folder-id}.

name: get-upload-url
